title: Is It Too Late To Stop Climate Change? Well, it's Complicated.

blocks.en_text: Climate change is just too much.
blocks.zh_text: 气候变化实在太让人头疼了。

blocks.en_text: There's never any good news.
blocks.zh_text: 从来就没有什么好消息。

blocks.en_text: Only graphs that get more and more red and angry.
blocks.zh_text: 只有越来越红、越来越刺眼的图表。

blocks.en_text: Almost every year breaks some horrible record,
blocks.zh_text: 几乎每年都会打破某项可怕的纪录，

blocks.en_text: from the harshest heat waves
blocks.zh_text: 从最猛烈的热浪

blocks.en_text: to the most rapid glacier melt.
blocks.zh_text: 到最快的冰川融化。

blocks.en_text: It's endless,
blocks.zh_text: 没完没了，

blocks.en_text: and relentless.
blocks.zh_text: 而且毫不留情。

blocks.en_text: We've known for decades that rapid climate change has been caused by the release of greenhouse gases.
blocks.zh_text: 几十年来我们就已经知道，快速的气候变化是由温室气体的排放造成的。

blocks.en_text: But instead of reducing them, in 2019 the world was emitting 50% more CO₂ than in the year 2000.
blocks.zh_text: 但温室气体不但没有减少，2019年全球的二氧化碳排放量反而比2000年多了50%。

blocks.en_text: And emissions are still rising.
blocks.zh_text: 而且排放量还在持续上升。

blocks.en_text: Why is that? Why is it so hard to just stop emitting these gases?
blocks.zh_text: 为什么会这样？为什么就是很难停止排放这些气体呢？

blocks.en_text: Our collective CO₂ emissions can be expressed as a product of four factors and their relationship with each other.
blocks.zh_text: 我们总的二氧化碳排放量可以表示为四个因素的乘积，以及它们彼此之间的关系。

blocks.en_text: Two of them explain why worldwide CO₂ emissions are still rising, and two explain how we can stop that.
blocks.zh_text: 其中两个因素解释了为什么全球二氧化碳排放量仍在上升，另外两个则说明了我们怎样才能阻止这种上升。

blocks.en_text: Population Size, Economic Growth, Energy Intensity, and Emissions pere Energy unit produced.
blocks.zh_text: 人口规模、经济增长、能源强度，以及每单位能源产生的排放量。

blocks.en_text: Number 1: Population Size
blocks.zh_text: 第一：人口规模

blocks.en_text: People need food, homes, and clothing.
blocks.zh_text: 人们需要食物、住房和衣服。

blocks.en_text: And they demand luxury products from iPhones to one dollar cheeseburgers
blocks.zh_text: 而且他们还想要各种奢侈品，从iPhone到一美元的芝士汉堡。

blocks.en_text: more people = higher CO₂ emissions.
blocks.zh_text: 人越多 = 二氧化碳排放越多。

blocks.en_text: It's a very simple equation.
blocks.zh_text: 这是个非常简单的等式。

blocks.en_text: The global population is growing, and according to the UN it will level off at about 11 billion in 2100, which is 40% more than today.
blocks.zh_text: 全球人口正在增长，根据联合国的预测，到2100年将稳定在约110亿，比现在多40%。

blocks.en_text: The only way to slow down this growth is investment in healthcare, and access to contraception and education in developing countries.
blocks.zh_text: 要减缓这种增长，唯一的办法是投资医疗保健，并让发展中国家的人们能获得避孕措施和教育。

blocks.en_text: But even with massive investment, it will take a few decades for the effects of lower birthrates to manifest themselves,
blocks.zh_text: 但即使投入大量资金，出生率下降的效果也要几十年才能显现出来，

blocks.en_text: so the global population will keep growing for the foreseeable future,
blocks.zh_text: 所以在可预见的未来，全球人口还会继续增长，

blocks.en_text: and, as a consequence, global CO₂ emissions rise over the next few decades.
blocks.zh_text: 因此，未来几十年全球二氧化碳排放量也会上升。

blocks.en_text: Number 2: Growth, or "Getting Richer".
blocks.zh_text: 第二：增长，或者说“变得更富有”。

blocks.en_text: But it's not just about our numbers,
blocks.zh_text: 但这不只是人口数量的问题，

blocks.en_text: The richer and more developed we are, the more emissions our lifestyle produces.
blocks.zh_text: 我们越富有、越发达，我们的生活方式产生的排放就越多。

blocks.en_text: A programmer in the US has a higher CO₂ footprint than 50 farmers in Uganda.
blocks.zh_text: 美国一个程序员的二氧化碳足迹比乌干达50个农民加起来还多。

blocks.en_text: The world's wealth is growing almost everywhere.
blocks.zh_text: 世界上几乎每个地方的财富都在增长。

blocks.en_text: And although it's far from easily distrubuted, economic growth has led to the highest standards of living, and the largest reduction in extreme poverty in human history.
blocks.zh_text: 虽然财富远未平均分配，但经济增长带来了人类历史上最高的生活水平，以及极端贫困的最大幅度减少。

blocks.en_text: Growth has become the dominant mantra of the world's economies, no matter what kind of political system they have.
blocks.zh_text: 增长已经成为世界经济体的主导信条，无论它们实行什么样的政治制度。

blocks.en_text: It's unlikely that rich countries will give up the concept of growth any time soon.
blocks.zh_text: 富裕国家不太可能在短期内放弃增长这个概念。

blocks.en_text: But even if they were to, developing countries want to become rich too
blocks.zh_text: 但就算他们愿意，发展中国家也想变富裕

blocks.en_text: For billions of people, the end of growth would probably mean staying poor
blocks.zh_text: 对数十亿人来说，增长的终结很可能意味着继续贫穷

blocks.en_text: and so developing countries are not willing to stop growing their economies.
blocks.zh_text: 所以发展中国家不愿意停止经济增长。

blocks.en_text: All in all, we can agree that growth as a guiding economic ideology is not going to go away any time soon.
blocks.zh_text: 总而言之，我们可以达成共识：把增长当作指导性经济意识形态，短期内是不会消失的。

blocks.en_text: More countries and their citizens around the world will grow and become richer while the rich economies will continue to grow their wealth.
blocks.zh_text: 世界上更多的国家和它们的公民会发展、变富，而富裕经济体也会继续增长财富。

blocks.en_text: There are some signs that growth can be decoupled from CO₂ emissions but we're not close to that yet.
blocks.zh_text: 有一些迹象表明，增长可以和二氧化碳排放脱钩，但我们离那一步还很远。

blocks.en_text: As a consequence of this growth, CO₂ emissions will rise.
blocks.zh_text: 这种增长带来的后果就是，二氧化碳排放会上升。

blocks.en_text: Ok, so far we've learned that because of population growth and economic growth, humanity's CO₂ emissions will increase.
blocks.zh_text: 好，到目前为止我们了解到，由于人口增长和经济增长，人类的二氧化碳排放会增加。

blocks.en_text: ...which is the opposite of what should be happening.
blocks.zh_text: ……而这和本该发生的情况正好相反。

blocks.en_text: We need to slow, peak, and then reduce annual emissions.
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要让年排放量放缓、达到峰值，然后再降下来。

blocks.en_text: The next two factors describe how we can actually do this.
blocks.zh_text: 接下来的两个因素讲的是我们究竟怎样才能做到这一点。

blocks.en_text: Number 3: Energy Intensity
blocks.zh_text: 第三点：能源强度

blocks.en_text: Energy intensity describes how efficiently we use energy.
blocks.zh_text: 能源强度描述的是我们使用能源的效率有多高。

blocks.en_text: A street food vendor in rural Brazil might burn coal to cook...
blocks.zh_text: 巴西农村的一个街头小吃摊贩可能烧煤来做饭……

blocks.en_text: while a street food vendor in France might use an induction stove powered by nuclear energy.
blocks.zh_text: 而法国的一个街头小吃摊贩可能用核能供电的电磁炉。

blocks.en_text: The latter is way more efficient.
blocks.zh_text: 后者效率高得多。

blocks.en_text: The more efficient something is, the less energy we need to do something.
blocks.zh_text: 某样东西效率越高，我们做某件事需要的能源就越少。

blocks.en_text: Be it powering a metropolitan area, or grilling a kebab.
blocks.zh_text: 不管是给一个大都市区供电，还是烤一串烤肉。

blocks.en_text: So making our technology more efficient, and coming up with more efficient ways to organise our societies
blocks.zh_text: 所以，让我们的技术更高效，想出更高效的方式来组织我们的社会

blocks.en_text: is one of the most important ways to reduce the modern world's CO₂ dependancy.
blocks.zh_text: 是减少现代世界对二氧化碳依赖的最重要方式之一。

blocks.en_text: This can mean everything from reducing power consumption with A.I.,
blocks.zh_text: 这可以意味着一切，从用人工智能降低能耗，

blocks.en_text: the electrification of the transportation and industrial sectors,
blocks.zh_text: 到交通和工业部门的电气化，

blocks.en_text: or sustainable concrete production.
blocks.zh_text: 再到可持续的混凝土生产。

blocks.en_text: The opportunities for improvement are almost limitless,
blocks.zh_text: 改进的机会几乎无穷无尽，

blocks.en_text: and human ingenuity can run wild.
blocks.zh_text: 人类的聪明才智可以尽情发挥。

blocks.en_text: But we know that increasing efficiency alone will not be enough,
blocks.zh_text: 但我们知道，仅仅提高效率是不够的，

blocks.en_text: mostly for 3 reasons:
blocks.zh_text: 主要有三个原因：

blocks.en_text: 1: Direct Rebound Effects.
blocks.zh_text: 1：直接反弹效应。

blocks.en_text: This means that once something becomes more efficient, it's used more,
blocks.zh_text: 意思是，一旦某样东西变得更高效，它就会被用得更多，

blocks.en_text: and so overall, the increased efficiency does not lead to a reduction as impressive as you would first think.
blocks.zh_text: 所以总体来看，效率提高带来的减排并没有你一开始想的那么可观。

blocks.en_text: ...or worse, sometimes more efficiency makes humans use not *less* of a resource,
blocks.zh_text: ……或者更糟，有时候效率提高反而让人用的资源不是*更少*，

blocks.en_text: but *more* of it.
blocks.zh_text: 而是*更多*。

blocks.en_text: When planes became more fuel-efficient, ticket prices decreased, and more people started to travel by plane.
blocks.zh_text: 当飞机变得更省油时，机票价格下降了，坐飞机出行的人也变多了。

blocks.en_text: So making things more efficient does not automatically mean less energy use in total.
blocks.zh_text: 所以，提高效率并不自动意味着总能耗会减少。

blocks.en_text: It might have the opposite effect.
blocks.zh_text: 它可能产生相反的效果。

blocks.en_text: 2: Indirect Rebound Effects.
blocks.zh_text: 2：间接反弹效应。

blocks.en_text: Sometimes when you save money on a thing that becomes more efficient, you might spend it elsewhere.
blocks.zh_text: 有时候，当你在某件变得更高效的东西上省了钱，你可能会把钱花到别处去。

blocks.en_text: For example, if you buy a more fuel-efficient car,
blocks.zh_text: 比如，如果你买了一辆更省油的车，

blocks.en_text: you save money on fuel, and end up with extra funds in your bank account...
blocks.zh_text: 你在燃油上省了钱，结果银行账户里多出了一笔钱……

blocks.en_text: ...that you might spend on vacation, and take a flight with.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能会拿这笔钱去度假，还坐飞机出行。

blocks.en_text: So in the end, you might actually emit more CO₂
blocks.zh_text: 所以到头来，你实际上可能排放了更多二氧化碳，

blocks.en_text: despite getting a more efficient car.
blocks.zh_text: 尽管你开的是一辆更高效的车。

blocks.en_text: 3: And lastly,
blocks.zh_text: 3：最后一点，

blocks.en_text: the more you optimise for efficiency,
blocks.zh_text: 你越是追求效率优化，

blocks.en_text: the harder and more expensive it becomes to get more efficient.
blocks.zh_text: 想要进一步提高效率就越难、越贵。

blocks.en_text: So, over time, the return on investment slows down.
blocks.zh_text: 所以，随着时间推移，投资回报会逐渐放缓。

blocks.en_text: And, with many technologies, we are already pretty efficient.
blocks.zh_text: 而且，在很多技术上，我们已经相当高效了。

blocks.en_text: But, regardless of how efficient we make our economies,
blocks.zh_text: 但是，无论我们把经济搞得多高效，

blocks.en_text: as long as we need at least some energy, we will have emissions.
blocks.zh_text: 只要我们至少还需要一些能源，就会有排放。

blocks.en_text: Efficiency alone won't create a zero-carbon world.
blocks.zh_text: 光靠效率无法创造零碳世界。

blocks.en_text: This brings us to our last factor:
blocks.zh_text: 这就引出了我们的最后一个因素：

blocks.en_text: Number 4: CO₂ emissions per energy unit used, or "Our Global Carbon Footprint".
blocks.zh_text: 第4点：每单位能源使用所产生的二氧化碳排放，也就是“我们的全球碳足迹”。

blocks.en_text: Humanity's global carbon footprint
blocks.zh_text: 人类的全球碳足迹

blocks.en_text: is the CO₂ released per energy unit generated.
blocks.zh_text: 就是每产生一单位能源所释放的二氧化碳。

blocks.en_text: For example, coal plants release much much more CO₂
blocks.zh_text: 比如，燃煤电厂释放的二氧化碳要多得多，

blocks.en_text: than solar power per unit of energy.
blocks.zh_text: 远超太阳能每单位能源的排放。

blocks.en_text: This relationship is crystal clear.
blocks.zh_text: 这种关系再清楚不过了。

blocks.en_text: The more fossil fuels we burn, the higher our CO₂ output.
blocks.zh_text: 我们燃烧的化石燃料越多，二氧化碳排放就越高。

blocks.en_text: Fossil fuels are the greatest lever humanity has right now.
blocks.zh_text: 化石燃料是人类目前最有力的杠杆。

blocks.en_text: Of course, it's impossible to shut down coal and oil overnight
blocks.zh_text: 当然，不可能一夜之间关停煤炭和石油，

blocks.en_text: without throwing society into chaos.
blocks.zh_text: 而不让社会陷入混乱。

blocks.en_text: But the reality is, that we're not doing nearly enough to keep fossil fuels in the ground
blocks.zh_text: 但现实是，我们在把化石燃料留在地下方面做得远远不够，

blocks.en_text: and use lower-carbon alternatives
blocks.zh_text: 也不够努力去使用低碳替代品。

blocks.en_text: We need to do 2 things to speed the transition away from fossil fuels.
blocks.zh_text: 要加快摆脱化石燃料的转型，我们需要做两件事。

blocks.en_text: First, we need to use the real leverage we have today, with today's technology
blocks.zh_text: 第一，我们需要用今天的技术，发挥我们当下真正拥有的杠杆作用。

blocks.en_text: There are a lot of things we can do extremely quickly.
blocks.zh_text: 有很多事情我们可以极快地做到。

blocks.en_text: We can leave nuclear power plants online longer.
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以让核电站运行更长时间。

blocks.en_text: We can cut subsidies to the fossil fuel industry,
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以削减对化石燃料行业的补贴，

blocks.en_text: and funnel them into renewables.
blocks.zh_text: 把它们投入到可再生能源上。

blocks.en_text: We can price carbon emissions harshly,
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以对碳排放严厉定价，

blocks.en_text: and increase the price each year
blocks.zh_text: 并且每年提高价格，

blocks.en_text: to create strong incentives for the world's industries to transition.
blocks.zh_text: 从而为全球各行业转型创造强有力的激励。

blocks.en_text: We can enforce strict standards for energy efficiency,
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以对能源效率执行严格标准，

blocks.en_text: and for any type of new construction.
blocks.zh_text: 对任何类型的新建项目也是如此。

blocks.en_text: We can phase out fossil fuel vehicles.
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以逐步淘汰化石燃料车辆。

blocks.en_text: Next, we also need to invent new and better technology.
blocks.zh_text: 接下来，我们还需要发明新的、更好的技术。

blocks.en_text: Without new technologies and innovation,
blocks.zh_text: 如果没有新技术和创新，

blocks.en_text: it will be impossible to achieve a zero CO₂ emission world,
blocks.zh_text: 就不可能实现一个零二氧化碳排放的世界，

blocks.en_text: be it from technologies like carbon capture,
blocks.zh_text: 无论是碳捕集这样的技术，

blocks.en_text: or a new generation of nuclear power plants,
blocks.zh_text: 还是新一代的核电站，

blocks.en_text: to new batteries that revolutionise the energy storage from renewables.
blocks.zh_text: 再到彻底改变可再生能源储能方式的新型电池。

blocks.en_text: But innovation takes time: years, and decades...
blocks.zh_text: 但创新需要时间：几年，甚至几十年……

blocks.en_text: ...and we don't have this time.
blocks.zh_text: 而我们没有这么多时间。

blocks.en_text: Every year, we keep adding more carbon to the atmosphere.
blocks.zh_text: 每一年，我们都在向大气中排放更多的碳。

blocks.en_text: This means we can't keep relying on innovation alone.
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着我们不能只依赖创新。

blocks.en_text: We need to find ways to reduce emissions today, while we invent what we will need in the future.
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要在发明未来所需技术的同时，找到今天就能减少排放的办法。

blocks.en_text: The less fossil fuel we burn over the next few years,
blocks.zh_text: 未来几年我们燃烧的化石燃料越少，

blocks.en_text: the more time we give innovation to catch up.
blocks.zh_text: 我们给创新追赶的时间就越多。

blocks.en_text: The more low-carbon energy infrastructure we build today,
blocks.zh_text: 我们今天建成的低碳能源基础设施越多，

blocks.en_text: the more we can compensate for economic growth, and the people born today.
blocks.zh_text: 我们就越能抵消经济增长和今天出生的人所带来的影响。

blocks.en_text: The more coal power plants in construction we stop from being finished,
blocks.zh_text: 我们阻止建成的燃煤电厂越多，

blocks.en_text: the more CO₂ we save.
blocks.zh_text: 我们节省的二氧化碳就越多。

blocks.en_text: Neither innovation, nor the alternatives we're using today alone
blocks.zh_text: 无论是创新，还是我们今天使用的替代方案，单靠任何一方

blocks.en_text: can solve rapid climate change.
blocks.zh_text: 都无法解决快速的气候变化。

blocks.en_text: But, innovation, together with a decisive move away from fossil fuels where it's possible today
blocks.zh_text: 但是，创新，加上在今天可行的领域果断摆脱化石燃料

blocks.en_text: could do it.
blocks.zh_text: 就能做到。

blocks.en_text: Solving climate change will be complicated.
blocks.zh_text: 解决气候变化会很复杂。

blocks.en_text: We have to account for the needs of billions of people
blocks.zh_text: 我们必须考虑到数十亿人的需求

blocks.en_text: and the reality that right now, society runs mostly on fossil fuels.
blocks.zh_text: 以及这样一个现实：目前社会主要依靠化石燃料运转。

blocks.en_text: This will not change overnight,
blocks.zh_text: 这不会一夜之间改变，

blocks.en_text: but it needs to change as quickly as possible.
blocks.zh_text: 但需要尽可能快地改变。

blocks.en_text: And it is still very much possible🤞🏻
blocks.zh_text: 而且这仍然非常有可能🤞🏻

blocks.en_text: We'll look at different aspects of climate change, and how to solve it
blocks.zh_text: 我们将探讨气候变化的各个方面，以及如何解决它

blocks.en_text: in more videos.
blocks.zh_text: 在更多视频中。

blocks.en_text: Let us know what kind of stuff you want to know more about
blocks.zh_text: 告诉我们你想了解更多哪方面的内容

blocks.en_text: Here on YouTube, or join us in our subreddit
blocks.zh_text: 在YouTube上，或者加入我们的subreddit
